text.p: Bausch & Lomb on Wednseday announced a restructuring it expects to result in annual savings of more than $100 million in 1999.
The company estimated that the program will cost approximately $80 million before taxes to implement over the course of 1997 and 1998.

In addition to a $12.8 million pre-tax charge against first quarter earnings, the company said it expects to recognize approximately $55-$60 million in restructuring costs by the end of 1997, the majority of which are expected to be recorded in the second quarter.

The company said when fully implemented, the various restructuring measures would eliminate approximately 1,900 jobs worldwide. However, the number of jobs lost would be partially offset by new employment positions created through the reinvestment made possible by the actions, along with expected growth in some segments of the company, such as contact lens manufacturing.

It said the initiatives will be implemented over the next two years. Approximately one third of the savings will be generated from restructuring projects related to the company's manufacturing processes.

Those projects are expected to result in improved operating margins, particularly in the eyewear business. The remainder of the savings will come from restructuring administrative functions, Bausch said.

The company said the savings generated are incremental to annual savings of $50 million that the company had identified through projects announced in early 1996. The company said that these existing plans are on track.

Bausch & Lomb said it plans to phase out sunglass component manufacturing at the company's Frame Center in Rochester, N.Y., and to "optimize" manufacturing operations in the sunglass global product delivery centers located in San Antonio, Texas; Waterford, Ireland; and Hong Kong.
The company said another objective of the restructuring is to align the company's organization to support Bausch & Lomb's strategy of managing its core eye care businesses on a global basis.

Including previous restructuring charges and writeoffs, the company reported net earnings for the quarter of $3.3 million, or $0.06 per share, compared with earnings in the same period last year of $22.5 million, or $0.39 per share.
